identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a Toyota 8FGU25 propane forklift (unit FL-2) covering September 2026, recording daily pre-shift checks of 12 safety items per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The log shows inspections completed on most days with one defect (horn failure on Sep 9) and multiple missing inspection records from Sep 3–6, despite evidence the truck was in operation during that gap.
scan.freshness_note: Current as of Sep 18, 2026. This is a monthly log still in use. Supervisor review signature and date fields on page 2 remain blank and should be completed.

gaps.title: Missing inspections Sep 3–6
gaps.description: No inspection records exist for Sep 3, 4, 5, or 6, 2026. The hour meter reading shows the truck ran during this period (4,819 hours on Sep 2 to 4,834 hours on Sep 7), proving the truck was in use. OSHA requires examination before each shift. The regulation does not permit gaps.
gaps.fix: Conduct a retroactive investigation to determine if inspections were actually performed but not recorded. If not performed, document this as a compliance failure and implement process to ensure inspections are not missed going forward. If performed, complete the missing log entries retroactively with the operator's identification and date completed.
gaps.locator: page 1-2, log entries Sep 3–6 not present
gaps.quote: Before being put into use and at least daily, powered industrial trucks shall be examined by the person designated to operate the truck

gaps.title: Horn defect not documented as resolved
gaps.description: On Sep 9, operator M.C. recorded a horn defect (X mark with note 'Horn not working'). On Sep 10 and subsequent dates, the horn column shows checkmarks. There is no note indicating when or how the horn was repaired, whether the truck was taken out of service, or supervisor approval for the repair. OSHA requires that trucks with defects affecting safety not be used.
gaps.fix: Complete the Sep 9 notes to document: (a) what action was taken (truck removed from service, repair ordered, repair completed), (b) date and time the truck was returned to service, (c) name of person who authorized return to service, (d) confirmation that repair was made by a qualified person. Add this information before Sep 10 entry if horn was repaired between Sep 9 and Sep 10.
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 entry 'Horn not working' note; page 1, Sep 10 entry shows horn passed
gaps.quote: do not use if a defect affects safety

gaps.title: Supervisor review signature missing
gaps.description: Page 2 shows a blank line for 'Supervisor review: ____________________ Date: __________' with no signature or date entered. This log is now complete through Sep 18 and should be signed off by a supervisor. While OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) does not explicitly mandate a supervisor signature on the log itself, a supervisor's review and authorization that the log is accurate and the truck is safe is an industry standard safety control.
gaps.fix: Have the supervisor responsible for the Portland warehouse sign and date the log to indicate review and approval of the inspection records. This should be done promptly after the last inspection (Sep 18) is recorded.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the findings about missing inspection records (Sep 3–6) and unresolved horn defect (Sep 9–10). The hour meter reading plainly shows the truck was used during the gap, and the regulation is unambiguous. The horn defect gap is clear from the transition from 'X' to 'checkmark' without documentation of repair. The supervisor signature gap is certain—the field is blank. All three gaps match the open findings already identified. Medium confidence in identifying whether Oregon OAR 437-004-0750 applies to the supervisor signature requirement; the federal OSHA rule does not explicitly require it, but signature is standard practice. I did not search for current Oregon rules and relied on the citation provided in the open findings. The document is legible and complete otherwise.
